synthesis:draft.headline: AEMO derives POE10 and POE90 operational-demand forecasts by scaling the POE50 operational-demand forecast.

document_statements.quote: The 10% and 90% POE forecasts are derived from the 50% POE forecast.
The 10% and 90% POE forecast are produced by multiplying the 50% POE forecast by a scaling factor.
A different scaling factor may be specified for each half-hour of the short term period.
The 10% and 90% scaling factors are based on statistical analysis of historical load and forecast data.

document_statements.paraphrase: The POE demands used in PDPASA and STPASA are derived from a forecast operational demand calculated by AEMO’s Demand Forecasting System (DFS) and AWEFS/ASEFS outputs.

document_statements.quote: OPERATIONAL_DEMAND_POE10 (number(15,2)): 10% probability of exceedance operational demand forecast value.
OPERATIONAL_DEMAND_POE50 (number(15,2)): 50% probability of exceedance operational demand forecast value.
OPERATIONAL_DEMAND_POE90 (number(15,2)): 90% probability of exceedance operational demand forecast value.
Process MTPASA uses 10% and 50% POE operational demand forecasts for modelling.

uncertainties: The retrieved passages state that 10% and 90% POE forecasts are produced by scaling POE50 and that scaling factors are based on statistical analysis, but they do not show the numerical scaling-factor values or how frequently those factors are updated.
The passages confirm that MTPASA uses 10% and 50% POE forecasts, but do not make clear whether the same short-term scaling method applies to MTPASA POE10 generation.
missing_evidence: Numerical values of the half-hourly scaling factors used to produce POE10 and POE90 from POE50 and any published table of those factors.
A detailed methodological description or appendix that publishes the statistical procedures used to derive the scaling factors and their update frequency.
Explicit documentation stating whether the same scaling-factor approach is used for MTPASA POE10/POE50 or if another method is used for medium-term forecasts.
